newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBM S.Africa hit at start by profit warning.
newsitem.headline: IBM S.Africa hit at start by profit warning.

text.p: A severe profit warning whacked shares in IBM South Africa Ltd to a new year low at the start of trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
The group announced earlier on Wednesday it expected to show a substantial trading loss for the six months' period ending June 30, 1997.

With only one trade of 200 shares by 0834 GMT, IBM fell 60 cents to 12.20 rand, replacing a previous year low of 12.60 and making it the eighth biggest percentage loss on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"It's hit by the profit warning. Pretty scary stuff and is down quite a bit, albeit in very thin trade," one dealer said.
The computer firm also announced it would restructure to improve focus on higher growth areas in a bid to better its competitiveness.
Recently-appointed managing director Sal Faso said in a published announcement that added to the trading loss in the interim period, there will be further costs associated with the restructuring.
Dealers said it was likely that IBM shares would take a further knock on Wednesday.
"We're likely to see quite a big shake-up there. It's going to be down some more," a dealer said.

IBM earnings for the year ended December 31, 1996 fell 27 percent to 73.8 million rand following the unsuccessful introduction of a new low-tier personal computer product. The product has been withdrawn.
